newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish board outlines new brokerage regulations.
newsitem.headline: Turkish board outlines new brokerage regulations.

text.p: Turkey's regulatory Capital Markets Board (SPK) introduced new regulations in pursuit of an August decree obliging banks in Turkey to set up or buy separate brokerage houses to handle their share transactions from January 2, 1997.

In its weekly bulletin published at the weekened, the SPK said if banks form new brokerages with at least 500 billion lira initial capital, 250 billion lira of it will be placed in Treasury bills and bonds to be kept at Istanbul Stock Exchange Settlement and Custody Bank, Takasbank.
But if they set up smaller scale brokerages with a 125 billion lira minimum capital, 100 billion lira of it will be blocked by Takasbank.
Banks will not be required to meet the minimum capital limits if they get ownership of an existing brokerage.
The SPK had taken measures for banks in August to conduct their capital market activities through brokerage houses in a move towards fair competition.
Some bankers had criticised the SPK for not consulting the banks and Treasury which regulates banks, before the decision.

According to the new regulations, a bank which does not set up a new brokerage or buy an existing one will lose all its intermediary licenses except the ones to make T-bill repurchase and reverse repurchase deals on the Istanbul Stock Exchange's bond market and broker share trade outside the Exchange.

The banks who plan to set up a separate brokerage house must apply to the SPK until November 11, the statement said, adding that future applications by banks who are not currently interested in setting up or buying a brokerage will also be considered after January 2, 1997.
At present 62 banks and 101 brokerages are Exchange members. Activities of three brokerages are temporarily under suspension. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75 ATA EKS
